answer: Practically, the chain should cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because mesa only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. In practice thread is enforced by the ledger itself: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any hollow approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
